transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No, please do not use it at all until a qualified engineer has checked it, as a swollen and split battery is an active safety hazard. While you wait for parts, you can safely inspect the charger contacts on both the dock and the vacuum body to ensure they are clean and dry with no visible damage. Please keep the unit switched off and unplugged in a safe, cool place away from flammable materials until it is repaired.

reading.symptom: battery got really hot on charge and looks puffed up with plastic case split at the seam

plan: They asked: "Can I still use it till a new one comes?" - answer that first.

Safety: a battery hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "battery got really hot on charge and looks puffed up with plastic case split at the seam". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply.
